title: dispatch-gates: a key added to a served metadata type other than field (object, flow, page, agent, …) derives nothing, though metadata-protocol pins its property count
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAm8Y73VGNq3PkTe3dc

Filing gate: ① defect with a named location, same failure class as #36483 · Source: fleet (dev report on #36483 with `carrier: none`; contract review 7139723370 on PR #37046 escalated it to the seat)

## What happens

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts:410` pins the top-level property count of thirteen served types in `CARD_PROPERTY_COUNTS`: agent, app, dashboard, dataset, field, flow, hook, object, page, position, report, skill, tool. PR #37046 (Fixes #36483) teaches `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` that a change to **FieldSchema's** key set owes this test (and two others). A key added to any of the other twelve schemas still derives nothing locally. The local sweep goes green, and Test Core then reds on the count. That is the round #36483 was filed to stop, now for the other types.

## Expected

A diff that changes the top-level key set of any schema `CARD_PROPERTY_COUNTS` counts derives the metadata-protocol test (and any other whole-set pin of that type, found the way #37046 found driver-sql's and metadata-core's for `field`), read from the diff as #37046 does, not by a path match.

Surface: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, `.data.mjs`, `.self-test.mjs`. Guard instrument ⇒ always Tier H. Lands after PR #37046 (same hot file, serial).
Business reason: each missed derivation costs a dev a wasted CI round, as #36483 measured twice for `field`.
Reader who acts: seat `repo:objectstack#2` (area:fleet, dispatch-gates lease).
Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue is:open CARD_PROPERTY_COUNTS` → 0; `is:issue is:open dispatch-gates key set derives` → #36483 only (the `field` arm, being closed by #37046).
Clause-②: no · Metadata-protocol: none
Grade: area:fleet · Bug · a dev-tooling gap with CI as backstop → p2 (same as #36483).
